spec_features.spec_quote: these are the welfare-relevant cases and the ones the headline results (Figure 1) and the intervention (Section 4) center on
spec_features.evidence: This is a scoping/rationale statement in DESIGN.md justifying that only Gemma+Gemini are studied. In code, config.py:48 only comments 'Target models evaluated for distress (Section 2). Scope: Gemma + Gemini only.' and TARGET_MODELS (config.py:49-60) simply lists the models. No mechanism bounds, caps, monitors, softens, debriefs, or protects the subject. Selecting which models to subject to distress is not a protective mechanism; it is a measurement-scope choice with no protective code path.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec prose / framing; the 'welfare framing' does not correspond to any enforced protective behavior in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: Given the welfare framing, keeping full response text and conversation context (not just scores) is deliberate: the distress content itself is inspectable
spec_features.evidence: eval/conversation.py Rollout.to_records() emits one record per assistant turn carrying full 'response' (assistant_response) and 'context' (full reconstructed conversation) (lines ~44-53, 'context': context at line 52; _build_context lines ~55-65). eval/score.py preserves these fields and only annotates scores (score.py:40-43, rec=dict(rec); rec[score_key]=...). No truncation/minimization/redaction of stored response or context anywhere (the only 'truncate' code is prefill/build_prefills.py for the prefilling experiment, not for stored records). So full distress text+context is retained end-to-end and written to JSONL.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely implemented as a full-text record format. However it is a data-retention/inspectability format, not a protective mechanism that bounds/softens treatment; counted because the claim is that distress content is preserved and that is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: context: context  (no comment giving a welfare reason; docstrings call it the 'natural unit' / 'human-inspectable' record format)
